en.title: Whether the First k Numbers Form a Contiguous Permutation
en.description:
The array is a permutation of 1..n. For each k, determine whether some contiguous subarray contains exactly 1..k, each once, and output n values of 0/1 in order.

This site has made the standard input and output explicit; any range not given by the source is marked as this site's protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains the permutation; 1≤n≤100000.
en.output: Output a 01 string of length n.
en.explanation: Example 1: k=1, 3, 4 qualify; for k=2, 1 and 2 are separated by 3, so output 1011. Example 2: every prefix qualifies, so output 111. Example 3: 1 and 2 are not adjacent, so only k=1, 3 qualify; output 101.
hints: Add positions by value from 1 to n and maintain the leftmost and rightmost positions. When the interval length equals the number k added so far, these k positions are contiguous.
